refuted_claims.claim: BABELE PACKAGING: 'Babele 2.9.1 ... already ships Adventure defaultMappings, so all three packs can be shipped as Adventure-type translation files WITHOUT A CUSTOM MAPPING.'
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Adventure defaultMappings do exist, but they delegate Actors and Items to the default Actor/Item mappings, which for this system reach almost nothing. Default Item = {name, system.description.value, effects}. Default Actor = {name, system.details.biography.value, items, effects, tokenName}. The alienrpg system stores NONE of its prose at those paths — it uses system.notes, system.general.special.value, system.general.appearance.value, system.general.sigItem.value, system.attributes.comment.value, system.general.comment.value, system.details.*, system.header.*, system.attributes.capacity.value, system.attributes.class.value. Worse, the one default path that looks like a fit is a type mismatch: in alien-rpg-system, items[].system.description is a plain STRING (12 skill-stunts, 1957 chars), not {value:...}. Shipping with defaults would silently leave every actor and item string in English: CR 235,746 (actor.prose 103,626 + item.prose 86,831 + actor.embitem.prose 45,289) + SS 39,889 + SYS 2,347 = 277,982 chars — i.e. 100% of the non-journal, non-table inventory. Custom Actor and Item mappings are mandatory, not optional.
refuted_claims.evidence: C:\Users\Taka\AppData\Local\FoundryVTT\Data\modules\babele\script\mapping\default-mappings.js — "Item": {"name":"name","description":"system.description.value","effects":{...}} and "Actor": {"name":"name","description":"system.details.biography.value","items":{...},"effects":{...},"tokenName":{"path":"prototypeToken.name"}}. Verified module.json id=babele version=2.9.1. Verified SYS item system.description types = {str, NoneType}, and that no CR/SS item has any system.description key at all.

refuted_claims.claim: SS-T-CORERES: '6 of 7 are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the core-rules copies; only Critical injuries differs ... Reuse CR-T-CORERES wholesale.' (echoed in CR-T-CORERES as 'identical copies exist in alien-evolved-starter-set (7 tables)').
refuted_claims.why_wrong: Only 5 of the 7 are byte-identical. 'Critical injuries' differs (correctly flagged). But the 7th, 'Sub Table Critical Injuries on Xenomorphs' (2 results, 680 chars), has NO core-rules counterpart whatsoever — corerules' only 'Sub Table' rolltable is 'EV - Sub Table Facehugger Attacks'. Telling the owner to 'reuse wholesale' means 680 chars of genuinely new translation gets skipped, and the table is also absent from the CR-T-CORERES unit list so it is never assigned anywhere.

verdict: The quantitative spine of this report is genuinely solid and safe to build on; the advisory layer is not. I independently reproduced all three per-pack totals to the character (76,036 / 340,968 / 2,286,505; grand 2,703,509) under the report's own field selection, confirmed that the work units sum to those totals with zero drift per pack and per journal, confirmed the journal-page enumeration is complete (CR 112 pages/38 text, SS 38/20, SYS 1/1, all image captions genuinely empty), and — the claim I most expected to break — confirmed that every one of the 41 slice cut points lands exactly on an opening h2/h3 tag with zero mid-tag splits and boundary headings matching the stated labels. Several reuse claims I initially thought were wrong turned out right on fairer measurement (Map Pins really is 100% contained in Hope's Last Day; the 43% Starter Set Rules figure is well-calibrated; CM-88G Bison really does appear twice at 3,945 chars; 10 of 11 cross-pack tables really are byte-identical; the SYS changelog offset 53,657 is exact). Where it fails is in the conclusions drawn on top of those numbers, and one failure is serious: the assertion that the packs can ship as Adventure translation files without a custom mapping is wrong, because Babele's default Actor and Item mappings point at system.details.biography.value and system.description.value while this system stores everything elsewhere — roughly 278,000 chars, the entire actor and item inventory, would silently ship in English, and the SYS pack's system.description is a bare string that mismatches even the one plausible default path. Beyond that, three "no work here" claims would cause real content to be dropped (the Starter Set's Sub Table Critical Injuries on Xenomorphs has no core-rules twin yet is marked "reuse wholesale"; the zero-text rolltable set is 9 tables/165 results not 8/118), the name-keyed rTables hazard list omits three CR tables and the whole Starter Set despite being billed as the project's top risk, the anchor-phase estimate silently switches from raw to visible chars and so understates the serial critical path by 66–87% (196k raw, not ~118k), and about 4,110 chars of literal "[object Object]" placeholder plus ~1,024 chars of uninventoried sheet fields (adhocitems, spacecraft header block, scene region names, Buddy/Rival) sit inside the published figures. Practical guidance: take the totals, the unit decomposition, the slice boundaries and the page/table/blockquote census as verified and start work on them; re-derive the Babele packaging plan from scratch before writing a single mapping file; and re-audit the reuse map, the zero-text table list, and the cross-reference hazard list before any unit is marked "paste only" or handed to a translator.
